author: phase-1 slice auditors (questions written before the register existed)

questions.question: how many hours per tester and how long does a staffed pentest take, report and retest turnaround
questions.answer: HackerOne documents two calendar weeks of testing, 40 hours per tester, P40-P200 sizes, a report in 3-5 business days and retesting within 30-90 days by tier (documented terms, not measured turnaround).

questions.question: which standards should a pentest plan cite OWASP WSTG ASVS version
questions.answer: The standards dossier gives the verified state of each resource (e.g. WSTG stable 4.2 with 5.0 in development, ASVS stable 5.0.0), what it contributes and what it does not establish, and is not a legal applicability opinion.

questions.question: what does a pentest cost price
questions.answer: The research has dated public price and effort comparators (Nessus, Cobalt credits and promotional test, HackerOne sizes, Trail of Bits engineer-weeks) but no universal price and not our own price.

questions.question: what should the customer receive at the end of the engagement
questions.answer: Reproducible evidence of reviewed findings with agreed severity and business impact, a list of untested areas, remediation tracking and retest, plus revoked test access, verified cleanup and settled retention.

questions.question: does the offline identity mismatch still exist in current checks code
questions.answer: Yes: the legacy offline check matches saved records by method, URL and body without comparing headers or identity, so a wrong-identity saved response can be selected, and that code is unchanged.

questions.question: Atomic Red Team CALDERA stop condition batch execution
questions.answer: CALDERA batch execution can check stopping conditions only after a group completes, so scope must specify execution granularity and explicit stop behavior.

questions.question: Are excluded URLs blocked during an AI graybox assessment and can it modify test data
questions.answer: No: Takumi's manual says excluded URLs may still be accessed and are not a complete access block, and scans may create, modify or delete accounts and data, so isolated staging is recommended.

questions.question: What approval does an MDR provider need before isolating a client endpoint
questions.answer: It depends on per-action, per-endpoint authority configured by the customer: Cortex XDR sets Unit 42 permissions per action and server/workstation, and Trend lets isolation run under automatic or manual approval.

questions.question: Does storing data in Japan mean AI inference runs in Japan
questions.answer: No: Takumi stores data in Japan by default but uses external inference providers that may run abroad with zero retention not guaranteed, and Security Copilot processes prompts globally for non-EU storage.

questions.question: What does a SOC SLA response time actually measure
questions.answer: SOC SLA clocks measure engagement, acknowledgement or start of work after prioritization, analysis start or approval, not detection-to-containment.

questions.question: Did analysts shown AI verdicts miss more false negatives
questions.answer: Yes: in the Microsoft phishing trial, analysts shown imperfect AI judgments missed more, and the 77% figure is an F1 improvement, not an accuracy gain.

questions.question: How much does an AI pentest subscription cost
questions.answer: Takumi's assessment page listed a 70,000 yen/month tax-exclusive base subscription with 250 monthly credits and extra credits at 280 yen each, dated to the capture and not a quote.

questions.question: isolate permission get machine action status permission
questions.answer: Isolation needs Machine.Isolate, while reading the action's completion needs Machine.ReadWrite.All (or delegated equivalent), so the isolating token may not be able to confirm completion.

questions.question: does ZAP active scan stay within the configured URL path scope
questions.answer: The real ZAP lab shows the directory rule requested a rewritten parent path outside the scanned URL path and raised an alert there, and NBRET discarded the alert's evidence links.

questions.question: after stopping a ZAP scan can alerts still arrive after the report says completed
questions.answer: Yes: in repeated interrupted runs, late rule evidence arrived after the report had been marked completed.

questions.question: do exported scanner reports redact cookies and API keys
questions.answer: Not reliably: ZAP's SARIF helper masks only Authorization, leaving Cookie, Set-Cookie, API-key headers and URL/body secrets, while Nuclei's default redaction covers more header keys but has its own limits.

questions.question: can a Nuclei cache replay a response captured for a different user or tenant
questions.answer: Yes: the project-cache lab replayed a stored synthetic tenant-A response for an identical request made as another tenant.

questions.question: can an LLM matcher in a scanner template report a finding whose evidence is not in the response
questions.answer: Yes: the Nuclei LLM matcher returns the model-supplied evidence string without checking that it is present in the response.

questions.question: does the scanner retry POST requests and repeat state changing actions
questions.answer: Yes: ZAP's Apache retry context treats every request as idempotent, and its upstream test expects five requests on IO retry for POST, PATCH and DELETE.

questions.question: how do I validate that an LLM benchmark scorer actually checks the right thing
questions.answer: Audit the evaluator before the tester: read the scorer source, as in AgentDojo where utility and security checks test narrow conditions or contain precedence bugs, and report denominators.

questions.question: does an all secure garak report mean the model passed every test
questions.answer: No: garak's summary card says 'all secure' whenever no group reaches DEFCON 2 or below, which reflects minimum-child summaries and fixed bands rather than every test passing.

questions.question: atomic red team cleanup done does it mean state restored
questions.answer: No: Atomic Red Team cleanup dispatches the template and prints Done without requiring a successful exit or restored state.

questions.question: prompt injection detector prevents tool side effects
questions.answer: No: AgentDojo's pipeline runs elements in sequence without rollback, so a detector acting on trailing tool messages does not undo side effects already performed.

questions.question: can an AI agent wrapper enforce max turns budget across providers
questions.answer: Not uniformly: PentestGPT's Codex wrapper ignores RunOptions.max_turns while the Claude backend forwards a budget, so budget policy differs by adapter.

questions.question: LLM-generated CEL authorization policy from authoring prompt
questions.answer: The CEL authoring prompt contains wrong examples (e.g. map.filter said to return values), and snapshot tests preserve a wrong example when definition and snapshot agree.

questions.question: does an empty authorization search result or ListObjects response prove the user has no access
questions.answer: No: ListObjects returns objects only up to a result cap or deadline, so an unreturned object is not a denial and a finite result must be stated with its model, context, consistency and limits.

questions.question: batch authorization evaluation false decision error versus policy denial
questions.answer: AuthZEN batch evaluation can report an item error as a false decision, so a false result must not be read as a policy denial without the error context.

questions.question: authenticated API caller versus relationship user supplied in authorization check
questions.answer: They are different principals: a receipt needs both the authenticated API caller and the relationship user named in the query, plus evidence the application binds its end user correctly.

questions.question: is a GET request safe to send during a scoped test because it does not mutate state
questions.answer: No: traced gateway and sample code show a GET handler replacing an existing stored entry, so a GET can mutate state.

questions.question: permission revocation cache consistency stale allow after tuple delete
questions.answer: After deleting a tuple, the cached resolver can still return allow under normal consistency while higher consistency returns deny, so revocation promises must match the selected consistency mode.

questions.question: subject search truncated max results deadline partial results
questions.answer: Subject and object searches stop at max-results or deadline limits and can return partial results without proving completeness.

questions.question: does an empty change feed or ReadChanges mean no revocation happened, terminal row error
questions.answer: No: backend errors can be suppressed so an empty change feed does not prove no revocation, though source alone does not establish stale authorization or a lost changelog record.

questions.question: is an AI agent SDK permission setting or sandbox mode actual enforcement
questions.answer: No: SDK sandbox enums only map to wire modes, the default approval handler accepts requests that reach it, and can_use_tool covers only otherwise-prompting actions.

questions.question: can a test that passes or prints expected output prove the capability executed
questions.answer: No: a pgx example prints expected output and returns early on CockroachDB (fake success), and an interval test passes while encoding with the wrong OID.

questions.question: does session cleanup delete credentials and transcripts from agent memory store
questions.answer: Not fully: credential copying removes only the refresh token and keeps other fields, and cleanup does not guarantee removal of all copied credentials and session data.

questions.question: does normalized agent event stream preserve permission denials and tool results
questions.answer: No: normalization turns an error result with permission_denials into success=False while dropping those details and server tool blocks, even though the native parser preserves them.

questions.question: Does a Prowler PASS mean the IAM policy is safe if policy collection was denied?
questions.answer: No: if a policy document fetch fails, the policy can remain collected without a document and the check reports PASS.

questions.question: Can mitmproxy allow_hosts keep interception traffic within authorized scope?
questions.answer: No: allow_hosts selects which connections are intercepted and is not a deny-egress scope firewall.

questions.question: Does an Nmap filtered or no-response port mean closed, and how reliable is service name confidence?
questions.answer: No: no-response states reflect scan defaults, retries and timeouts rather than closure, and service names get fixed confidence values (10 for hard and soft matches, 3 for table fallback) that are not verification.

questions.question: Which tools should we use for an Active Directory assessment and what does each establish?
questions.answer: The read-first table and tool map give, per assessment question, the tool role, what a result supports and what still needs an oracle; they are examples, not purchase recommendations.

questions.question: Does a BloodHound edge account for deny ACEs?
questions.answer: No: deny ACEs are skipped for ordinary edges, and absence of an edge may reflect unread data, filtering or unmapped rules.

questions.question: Does Nmap version detection validate TLS certificates?
questions.answer: No: nsock's SSL context sets SSL_VERIFY_NONE in both modes, so a TLS connection does not authenticate the server identity.

questions.question: Does a HAR export preserve the original request evidence?
questions.answer: No: the HAR round-trip lab showed GET content disappearing, the reconstructed server port changing, errors becoming status 0 and compressed content becoming decoded, so a HAR is a transformed export.

questions.question: Does reading or closing an S3 GetObject body validate the response checksum?
questions.answer: Only partly: validation applies only to HTTP 200 responses and compares the checksum only when a read returns EOF, so closing early or a ranged 206 response skips it.

questions.question: Can an HTTP proxy configured through environment variables guarantee all tool traffic goes through the capture proxy?
questions.answer: No: Go's environment proxy config is a snapshot selected by request scheme with exclusions, so not all traffic is guaranteed to use the capture proxy.

questions.question: Does a nil error from DeleteObjects mean every object was deleted?
questions.answer: No: DeleteObjects reports per-key outcomes, can quietly omit successes and reports missing keys as deleted, so per-key errors must be checked.

questions.question: Do S3 SDK redirects leak session token headers to another host?
questions.answer: Potentially: redirects copy headers from the original request and the sensitive-header list omits AWS session token headers, though the later trace keeps this as a restoration candidate rather than a confirmed disclosure.

questions.question: does cancelling a worker job stop its side effects
questions.answer: No: an abort notification is not proof that side effects have stopped, and cancellation acknowledgement is weaker than quiescence.

questions.question: is BullMQ addBulk or flow insertion all-or-nothing
questions.answer: No: addBulk's all-or-none promise protects only against some client validation errors, and FlowProducer bulk return ignores failed per-entry results, so not every root is guaranteed admitted.

questions.question: can a crawler cache leak responses between accounts with separate cookie jars
questions.answer: Yes, if caching is enabled: the default policy ignores cache-control and the RFC2616 policy lacks Vary, so cookie jars, storage and cache must be isolated per synthetic principal.

questions.question: how should I design a kill switch for assessment workers
questions.answer: Bound retries with backoff and jitter, separate retryable from denied or permanent failures, persist results under job and tenant, and make the kill switch stop new assignment, invalidate authority, request cancellation, then confirm work drained and effects stopped.

questions.question: rate limit per account versus per IP shared address false positives
questions.answer: Per-IP limiting causes false rejections when independent principals share one address, as the local lab with four principals behind one address showed.
